purpose: Help Bridge Engine discover how each user learns best through preference questions, behavior, and task outcomes. This is not a fixed learning-style label system; it should adapt over time based on what actually works.
guardrail: Avoid boxing users into one learning style. Treat styles as flexible modes that change by task, energy level, context, and mood.

hands_on.label: Hands-on building
hands_on.task_pattern: Build or change something immediately, then explain what changed.

audio.label: Listening / audio
audio.task_pattern: Listen, repeat, summarize out loud, or record a short explanation.

walking.label: Walking / movement
walking.task_pattern: Take a short walk and answer one focused question verbally or in notes.

music_supported.label: Music-supported focus
music_supported.task_pattern: Use a playlist/timer and complete one short visible action.

visual.label: Visual diagrams / maps
visual.task_pattern: Sketch a map, flowchart, dashboard card, or diagram.

reading.label: Reading
reading.task_pattern: Read a tiny section, highlight the useful part, and apply it immediately.

writing.label: Writing / explaining
writing.task_pattern: Write a short explanation, checklist, script, or mini-summary.

social_teaching.label: Teaching / social explanation
social_teaching.task_pattern: Explain the concept to a friend, imaginary audience, or AI coach.

gamified.label: Challenge / game-style learning
gamified.task_pattern: Turn the next action into a challenge, unlock, score, or level-up.

discovery_questions.prompt: When do you usually focus best?
What makes a task easiest to start?
Which ways of learning feel most natural to you?
What helps your environment feel more doable?
What formats make you avoid starting?
